_doc: Revert-verify mutants for issue #4313 — the forget-leak guard had the same disease it guards against, one level up: (1) it read only `exocmd__Command_precondition` and was blind to a binding-level override, which REPLACES that tree at runtime (`CommandResolver.ts`), and (2) its lifecycle population was a hand-written literal set compared by exact string, so a binding on an un-enumerated class was absent from the population rather than misjudged. The subject is the guard test itself — it is a data-driven guard, so its classifier IS the mechanism. `red_re` anchors on the `● <suite> › P<n> …` header; the file's pre-existing axes are prose-named and deliberately out of the machine key space.
subject: <ABSOLUTE PATH TO YOUR exocortex CHECKOUT>/packages/core/tests/integration/dynamic-commands/PrototypePreconditionForgetGuard.test.ts

M1_bucket_is_a_rubber_stamp._note: The classifier accepts everything, so the ratchet can never report an unrecognised class. P2 stays green by construction — which is exactly why P3 exists.

M2_creation_bucket_removed._note: Back to name-based buckets only: ems__BookReadingSession (one binding, a create-from-prototype command) becomes unrecognised again — the very member the issue named.

M3_binding_override_ignored._note: The guard goes back to reading only the command-level precondition, so an override that drops the clause is invisible — the #4313 item-1 blindness.

M4_creation_bucket_accepts_any._note: One creation binding would excuse a class that ALSO carries lifecycle commands from the guard.

M5_lifecycle_binding_population_emptied._note: Canary check: with the population empty, P5 would pass vacuously — P4 is what catches that. Also reddens P6 by construction: P6 draws its sample binding from the same population, so an empty one leaves it nothing to override — which is itself the point P4 makes.
